## Natural history notes

A medium-sized wild cat characterized by its spotted brown to grayish coat, short “bobbed” tail, tufted ears, and long legs. In Florida, it is found in forests, pine flatwoods, hammocks, swamps, scrub, agricultural edges, and suburban natural areas with adequate cover. It is mostly active at night or around dawn and dusk, feeding mainly on rabbits, rodents, birds, and other small animals while relying on dense vegetation for stalking and shelter.
